correctness.rationale: For every integer q>=2, connected induced sides classify all facet cuts of K_{2,q}. A facet is a Euclidean orthogonal product of two induced graphical zonotopes, each with intrinsic volume sqrt(s) times its number of spanning trees. The two disjoint cut types yield 2q leaf facets of area (q-1)2^(q-2)sqrt(q+1) and 2 binomial(q,b) other facets of area sqrt((b+1)(q-b+1)) for b=0,...,q, with exact exhaustive counts. The resulting area and volume formulas follow. Binomial central moments through degree four and a deterministic square-root remainder bound prove the stated q^-3/2 surface concentration and surface/volume expansion. The packaged direct convex-hull program verifies all 74 individual facets for q=2,3,4, plus their total areas and volumes, and tests three larger binomial profiles; finite tests are not treated as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Against the accessible primary texts, the two-hub facet-area spectrum and surface-area condensation are not supplied by prior face-count, matrix-tree, deformation-cone, vertex-radius, or inball results. Existing general facet and volume formulas are explicitly credited as inputs; the new claim is the computed metric classification and quantitative area condensation for this specific canonical infinite family. The search cannot establish absolute historical uniqueness, and unindexed equivalent literature is a residual risk.
residual_risks: Generic zonotope and spanning-tree formulas make this special case computationally accessible; an earlier unindexed specialization or independently derived boundary area asymptotic remains possible.

value.rationale: The complete-bipartite two-hub graphical zonotope is a basic non-tree shuffle building block whose combinatorial facet count is known. The theorem determines every individual Euclidean facet measure and reveals that 2q facets, an exponentially vanishing fraction, carry 1-2q^(-3/2)+O(q^(-5/2)) of surface area. This resolves a natural geometric size-bias question with an exact quantitative rate and avoids asserting an arbitrary finite table or rebranding the known facet count as new.
